verses.text: This is the kickoff of the Good News of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
Just like the prophets said: God sending a messenger ahead to prep the road.
“A voice in the wilderness yelling: Clear the path for the Lord!”
John the Baptist pulled up in the wilderness preaching repentance and baptism for forgiveness.
People from Judea and Jerusalem were flooding to him, confessing their sins, getting baptized in the Jordan.
John’s fit was straight wilderness-core: camel drip, leather belt, and eating locusts + honey like a survival YouTuber.
He preached, “Someone stronger than me is coming. I’m not worthy to even untie His shoes fr.”
“I baptize with water—He’s baptizing with the Holy Ghost.”
Jesus came from Nazareth and got baptized by John in the Jordan.
As He came up, the heavens opened and the Spirit landed on Him like a holy dove download.
A voice said, “You’re my beloved Son. I’m proud of You.”
Immediately, the Spirit led Him into the wilderness.
He was there forty days, tempted by Satan, chilling with wild animals, and angels were serving Him.
After John got arrested, Jesus started preaching in Galilee, dropping the Gospel of God.
He said, “Time’s up. Kingdom is here. Repent and believe the good news.”
Walking by the sea, Jesus saw Simon and Andrew fishing.
He said, “Follow Me and I’ll turn you into fishers of people.”
They straight-up dropped their nets and followed.
He saw James and John with their dad fixing nets.
He called them too, and they dipped on the family boat immediately.
They went to Capernaum. On Sabbath, Jesus entered the synagogue and started teaching.
People were stunned—He taught with actual authority, not NPC energy like the scribes.
A man with an unclean spirit was there wilding.
The spirit screamed, “What do you want, Jesus of Nazareth? You here to destroy us? I know who You are—the Holy One of God!”
Jesus said, “Shut it. Come out.”
The demon convulsed the man, yelled, and dipped.
Everyone was shook: “Bro teaches with power AND commands demons?”
News about Him spread everywhere in the region.
After synagogue, they went to Simon and Andrew’s house with James and John.
Simon’s mother-in-law was sick with fever.
Jesus lifted her up, the fever left, and she immediately started serving dinner like nothing happened.
That evening people brought all the sick and demon-possessed.
The whole city crowded at the door.
Jesus healed many with diseases, cast out demons, and didn’t let them talk because they knew who He was.
Early morning, Jesus dipped out to a quiet spot to pray.
Simon and the squad started searching for Him.
They found Him and said, “Everyone’s looking for You.”
He said, “Let’s go to the other towns—I gotta preach there too. That’s why I came.”
He preached in their synagogues across Galilee and cast out demons.
A leper came kneeling, saying, “If You want, You can heal me.”
Jesus was moved, touched him, and said, “I want to. Be clean.”
Immediately the leprosy dipped.
Jesus told him strongly not to tell anyone.
“Go show yourself to the priest and do the Moses-level offerings as proof.”
But the man went out telling everybody, so Jesus couldn’t enter towns openly anymore and stayed in wilderness areas—yet people kept pulling up from everywhere.
Jesus came back to Capernaum, and word spread faster than TikTok drama that He was in the house.
The place got JAM-PACKED—zero space, not even at the door—so He started preaching to the whole mob.
Then four dudes pulled up carrying their paralysed friend like, “We getting you healed TODAY.”
Crowd too thick? They said “bet,” climbed the roof, ripped it open, and dropped their guy down right in front of Jesus—zero shame.
Jesus saw their insane faith and said to the man, “My guy, your sins? Cleared.”
Meanwhile some scribes sat there silently malding.
They were thinking, “Why He talking like that? Only God can forgive sins.”
Jesus read their minds instantly and said, “Why y’all thinking L thoughts in your hearts?”
“Which sounds easier—‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or ‘Get up and walk’?”
“But to prove I’ve got authority on earth to forgive sins…” He turned to the man,
“Bro. Get up, grab your mat, and go home.”
Man stood up IMMEDIATELY, picked his mat like it was light work, and walked out while the whole crowd went feral, glorifying God like, “We ain’t NEVER seen anything like this.”
Jesus dipped out again to the seaside, and the crowd followed Him like He was trending #1. He kept teaching them.
He saw Levi chilling at the tax booth and said, “Follow Me.” Levi stood up and didn’t even clock out—he just left.
Later Jesus was eating at Levi’s place with a whole squad of tax collectors and notorious sinners because yes, Jesus hangs with the people y’all judge.
Scribes and Pharisees saw it and started whining to His disciples, “Why He eating with THOSE people?”
Jesus heard it and said, “Healthy people don’t need a doctor. Sick people do. I didn’t come for the self-righteous—I came for the messy ones.”
John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting, so people asked Jesus, “Why Your disciples not fasting too?”
Jesus said, “The wedding squad doesn’t fast when the groom’s WITH them.”
“But when the groom gets taken away, THEN they’ll fast.”
“Nobody patches old clothes with fresh fabric—new cloth rips old cloth worse.”
“And nobody pours new wine into crusty old bottles—new wine will EXPLODE them. New wine goes in fresh bottles.”
One Sabbath, Jesus and His disciples were strolling through grainfields, and the disciples started plucking grain like a free snack.
Pharisees—professional fun police—said, “Why they doing what’s illegal on the Sabbath?”
Jesus replied, “Y’all remember David? When he was hungry and desperate…”
“He went into the house of God and ate the bread meant ONLY for priests—and gave some to his squad too.”
Then Jesus said, “The Sabbath was made to help humans—not humans built to serve the Sabbath.”
“So yeah, the Son of Man is LORD even over the Sabbath.”
Jesus rolled into the synagogue again, and there was a man with a dried-up hand.
The ops watched Jesus like hawks, waiting to see if He’d heal him on the Sabbath so they could accuse Him.
Jesus told the man with the weak hand, “Step forward.”
Then He asked the room, “What’s allowed on the Sabbath—doing good or doing evil? Saving a life or ruining one?” They stayed SILENT.
Jesus looked around at them, lowkey angry and disappointed at their stone hearts. Then He told the man, “Stretch your hand.” He did, and it was restored instantly.
The Pharisees stormed out and immediately started plotting with the Herodians on how to cancel Jesus permanently.
Jesus withdrew with His disciples to the sea, and a huge crowd followed Him from everywhere.
People from Judea, Jerusalem, Idumaea, across the Jordan, and around Tyre and Sidon pulled up because they heard the miracles He was doing.
He told His disciples to keep a small boat ready so the crowd wouldn’t crush Him.
He healed so many that people were pushing just to touch Him.
Whenever unclean spirits saw Him, they fell down and screamed, “You’re the Son of God!”
But He shut them down and told them not to expose Him.
Jesus went up a mountain and picked the ones He wanted; they pulled up to Him.
He appointed twelve so they’d stay close to Him and be sent out to preach,
with the authority to cast out demons.
Simon—He nicknamed him Peter.
James and John, sons of Zebedee—He nicknamed them “Boanerges,” meaning “Sons of Thunder.”
Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Canaanite,
and Judas Iscariot, who eventually betrayed Him.
They went into a house, and the crowd swarmed again so intensely they couldn’t even eat.
His family heard the chaos and said, “He’s out of His mind,” and tried to grab Him.
The scribes from Jerusalem said, “He’s possessed by Beelzebub,” claiming He cast out demons by the prince of demons.
Jesus called them over and hit them with parables: “How can Satan cast out Satan?”
“If a kingdom fights itself, it collapses.”
“If a house fights itself, it falls apart.”
“And if Satan’s divided, he’s finished.”
“No one can rob a strong man’s house unless they tie him up first; then they can clear the place out.”
“Truly, people can be forgiven for any sin or reckless speech…”
“But whoever trash-talks the Holy Spirit is committing a never-ending offense.”
He said that because they claimed He had an unclean spirit.
Then Jesus’ mother and brothers arrived and stood outside, sending for Him.
The crowd told Him, “Your family’s outside looking for You.”
Jesus replied, “Who is My mother? Who are My brothers?”
He looked around at the folks sitting near Him and said,
“These—who do the will of God—are My brother, My sister, and My mother.”
Jesus started teaching by the seaside again, and the crowd got so massive He hopped into a boat and sat while everyone stood on the shore.
He taught them many things in parables and said:
“Listen up: A sower went out to plant seed.”
“Some fell on the path, and birds swooped in and ate it.”
“Some fell on rocky ground—sprang up fast because the soil was shallow,”
“but when the sun hit, they dried out immediately because they had no roots.”
“Some fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked them out.”
“But some fell on good soil, grew strong, and produced thirty, sixty, and a hundredfold.”
Then He said, “If you’ve got ears, use them.”
When they were alone, the crew and others asked Him about the parable.
He said, “You’ve been given the mystery of God’s kingdom, but outsiders only get parables,”
“so that seeing they won’t really see, and hearing they won’t really hear or understand.”
He added, “If you don’t get this parable, how will you get the others?”
“The sower plants the word.”
“The ones on the path are those who hear, and immediately the enemy pulls up and steals the word from them.”
“The rocky-ground ones hear the word and receive it with hype,”
“but they have no root—so when pressure or trouble comes, they fall off instantly.”
“The thorny ones hear the word,”
“but life’s worries, riches, and desires choke it out, and it becomes useless.”
“But the good-soil ones hear, accept, and produce fruit—thirty, sixty, and a hundredfold.”
He said, “Nobody lights a lamp just to hide it under a basket or bed. You put it on a stand.”
“Everything hidden will eventually be revealed.”
“If you’ve got ears, listen.”
He said, “Pay attention to what you hear. With the measure you use, it’ll be measured back to you—and more.”
“Whoever has will receive more; whoever doesn’t have will lose even what they think they have.”
He said, “The kingdom of God is like a man who plants seed in the ground,”
“and sleeps and wakes, day after day, while the seed sprouts and grows—he doesn’t even know how.”
“The earth produces on its own: first the blade, then the head, then the full grain.”
“And when it’s ready, he harvests immediately.”
He said, “What can we compare the kingdom of God to? What parable fits?”
“It’s like a mustard seed—smallest of all seeds when planted,”
“but once grown, it becomes bigger than all the herbs, with branches large enough for birds to chill in its shade.”
He taught them many such parables, giving them as much as they could handle.
He didn’t speak to them without parables; but privately, He explained everything to His disciples.
That same day, when evening came, He said, “Let’s go to the other side.”
They sent the crowd away and took Him in the boat just as He was; other boats were with Him.
A violent storm hit—the waves were filling the boat fast.
Jesus was in the back, asleep on a cushion. They woke Him up panicking, “Teacher, don’t You care that we’re about to die?”
He got up, rebuked the wind, and told the sea, “Calm. Be still.” And the wind dropped instantly, and there was complete peace.
He said to them, “Why are you terrified? Where’s your faith at?”
They were shook and said to each other, “Who IS this, that even the wind and sea obey Him?”
They arrived on the other side of the sea, in the country of the Gadarenes.
As soon as Jesus stepped out the boat, a man with an unclean spirit sprinted out of the tombs toward Him.
The dude lived among tombs, and no one could hold him down anymore, not even with chains.
He’d been bound often with chains and shackles, but he snapped them like twigs, and no one could restrain him.
Night and day he wandered the mountains and tombs, crying out and cutting himself with stones.
When he saw Jesus far off, he ran and fell at His feet.
He shouted with a loud voice, “What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? Don’t torment me!”
Jesus had told the spirit, “Come out of the man.”
Jesus asked him, “What’s your name?” He replied, “Legion, because we’re many.”
He begged Jesus not to send them out of the region.
A large herd of pigs was feeding nearby on the hillside.
The demons begged Him, “Send us into the pigs so we can enter them.”
Jesus permitted them, and the spirits rushed out, entered the pigs, and the whole herd ran off a cliff into the sea and drowned.
The pig keepers ran off and told everyone in the city and countryside. People came to see what happened.
They found the man who’d been possessed—now sitting, clothed, and completely sane—and they got scared.
The eyewitnesses told them what happened to the man and the pigs.
The people begged Jesus to leave their region.
When Jesus got back into the boat, the healed man begged to come with Him.
Jesus didn’t allow it and said, “Go home and tell everyone how much the Lord has done for you and the mercy you received.”
So he went around the Decapolis telling everyone what Jesus did, and people were amazed.
Jesus crossed back to the other side, and a huge crowd gathered around Him near the sea.
A synagogue leader named Jairus showed up, fell at Jesus’ feet,
and begged Him: “My little daughter is at the point of death. Please come lay Your hands on her so she may live.”
Jesus went with him, and a massive crowd followed, pressing around Him.
A woman with a twelve-year flow of blood was there,
who’d suffered under many physicians, spent all her money, and only got worse.
She heard about Jesus and came behind Him in the crowd, touching His cloak.
She said to herself, “If I can just touch His clothes, I’ll be healed.”
Immediately the bleeding stopped, and she felt in her body she was healed.
Jesus instantly felt power go out of Him and asked, “Who touched my clothes?”
His disciples said, “Bro, You see this crowd? Everyone’s touching You.”
But He kept looking around to see who did it.
The woman, scared but honest, came forward and told Him everything.
He said, “Daughter, your faith healed you. Go in peace and be whole.”
While He was still speaking, people came from Jairus’ house saying, “Your daughter is dead. Don’t bother the Teacher anymore.”
Jesus heard it and said to Jairus, “Don’t fear. Just believe.”
He didn’t let anyone follow except Peter, James, and John.
They reached the house and saw chaos—people crying loudly.
Jesus said, “Why all this noise? The girl isn’t dead—she’s asleep.”
They laughed at Him, but He put them all out, took the parents and His three disciples, and went to where the child was.
He took her hand and said, “Talitha cumi,” meaning, “Little girl, I say to you, rise.”
Immediately the girl got up and walked—she was twelve—and everyone was shocked.
He told them strictly not to tell anyone and said to give her something to eat.
Jesus left there and went to His hometown, and His disciples followed Him.
When the sabbath came, He taught in the synagogue, and the people were shocked: “Where He get all this wisdom and power?”
“Isn’t this the carpenter, Mary’s son, with brothers James, Joses, Judah, and Simon? And His sisters are here too.” They got offended at Him.
Jesus said, “A prophet gets honor everywhere except his hometown, his relatives, and his own house.”
He could do only a few miracles there, healing a few sick people.
He marveled at their unbelief and went around teaching in the villages.
He called the Twelve and sent them out two by two, giving them authority over unclean spirits.
He told them to take nothing except a staff—no bag, no bread, no money.
Wear sandals, but don’t take extra clothes.
“Wherever you enter a house, stay there until you leave that place.”
“If people don’t receive you or listen to you, leave and shake the dust off your feet as a testimony against them.”
They went out and preached that people should repent.
They cast out many demons, anointed many sick people with oil, and healed them.
King Herod heard of Jesus—His name was spreading—and said, “John the Baptist is risen from the dead; that’s why He has this power.”
Others said, “He’s Elijah,” and others, “He’s a prophet like the ones before.”
But Herod said, “It’s John, whom I beheaded; he’s risen.”
Herod himself had arrested John, bound him, and put him in prison because of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife.
John had told Herod, “It isn’t lawful for you to have her.”
Herodias held a grudge and wanted him dead, but couldn’t,
because Herod feared John, knowing he was righteous and holy, and protected him. When he listened to him, he was troubled yet interested.
Then came Herod’s birthday feast. Herodias’s daughter danced and pleased Herod and the guests.
The king said, “Ask me anything, and I’ll give it.”
He swore, “Whatever you ask, up to half my kingdom.”
She asked her mother, “What should I request?” She said, “The head of John the Baptist.”
She hurried back and said, “I want John the Baptist’s head on a plate right now.”
The king was upset, but because of his oath and the guests, he didn’t refuse.
He ordered a soldier to bring John’s head. The soldier beheaded him in prison,
brought his head on a plate, and gave it to the girl, and she gave it to her mother.
John’s disciples came, took his body, and laid it in a tomb.
The apostles gathered to Jesus and told Him everything they’d done and taught.
He said, “Come aside to a quiet place and rest.” Crowds kept coming and going, and they didn’t even have time to eat.
They went away in a boat to a quiet place.
The crowd saw them leaving and ran ahead from all the cities, arriving before them.
Jesus saw them and was moved with compassion because they were like sheep without a shepherd. He taught them many things.
When it got late, the disciples said, “This place is empty and it’s getting dark,”
“Send them away so they can buy food.”
Jesus said, “You give them something to eat.” They said, “Should we buy bread for all these people??”
He said, “How many loaves do you have? Go check.” They said, “Five, and two fish.”
He told them to make everyone sit down on the grass in groups.
They sat in groups of hundreds and fifties.
Jesus took the loaves and fish, looked up, blessed them, broke them, and gave them to the disciples to distribute.
Everyone ate and was filled.
They collected twelve baskets full of leftovers.
About five thousand men ate.
Immediately Jesus made His disciples get into the boat and go ahead to Bethsaida while He dismissed the crowd.
After He sent them away, He went up the mountain to pray.
That night, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and He was alone on land.
He saw them struggling against the wind and came toward them walking on the sea, intending to pass by.
When they saw Him walking on the water, they thought He was a spirit and cried out,
because they all saw Him and were terrified. But He said, “Take courage; it’s Me. Don’t be afraid.”
He went into the boat, and the wind stopped. They were beyond astonished,
because they hadn’t understood the miracle of the loaves—their hearts were hardened.
They crossed over and came to Gennesaret and anchored there.
When they got out, people recognized Him immediately
and ran throughout that whole region bringing sick people on mats to wherever they heard He was.
Wherever He entered—villages, towns, or countryside—they placed the sick in the streets and begged to touch even the edge of His garment, and all who touched Him were healed.
Pharisees and some scribes came down from Jerusalem and watched Jesus’ disciples eating without the elders’ ritual hand-washing.
(For the Pharisees and all the Jews follow the tradition of the elders and never eat without washing their hands up to the wrist.)
They observed many other ritual washings—cups, pots, brazen vessels—because tradition is full checklist energy.
And when they come from the marketplace, they don’t eat without washing; plus there are many other man-made rules they follow.
So they asked Jesus, “Why don’t Your disciples walk according to the tradition of the elders but eat bread with unclean hands?”
He answered them, “Isaiah the prophet called you out perfect: ‘This people honors Me with their lips, but their heart is far from Me.’”
“You worship Me in vain, teaching doctrines that are just human commands.”
“You leave the commandment of God and cling to the tradition of men.”
“You do many things full well to make God’s command of none effect by your own rules.”
He said, “Moses commanded, ‘Honor your father and mother,’ and, ‘Whoever curses father or mother, let him die.’”
“But you say, ‘If a man says to his father or mother, “Whatever profit I might have received from you is Corban (a gift devoted to God),”’”
“then you allow him to do nothing for his parents, making the word of God of none effect by your tradition which you deliver.”
“You hypocrites! Well did Isaiah prophesy of you, saying,”—(repeat of the charge for emphasis).
Then Jesus called the multitude again and said, “Hear Me, everyone, and understand.”
“There is nothing from outside a man, entering into him, that can defile him; but the things which come out of him, those are the things that defile a man.”
If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear and actually listen.
When He was by Himself in the house, His disciples asked Him about the parable He gave.
He said to them, “Are you also without understanding? Do you not perceive?”
“Do you not understand that whatever enters into a man from outside cannot make him unclean?”
“For it does not enter into his heart, but into his belly, and goes out into the latrine—making all foods clean.”
And He said, “What comes out of a man is what defiles the man.”
“From within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,”
thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness.
“All these evil things come from within and defile the man.”
Then He went out from there and departed into the coasts of Tyre; He entered into an house and would have no man know it, trying to keep low.
But a certain woman whose young daughter had an unclean spirit heard of Him, and she came and fell at His feet.
The woman was a Greek, a Syrophoenician by nation; she besought Him to cast the devil out of her daughter.
He answered her, “Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the children’s bread and to cast it to the dogs.”
And she answered and said unto Him, “Yes, Lord: yet the dogs under the table eat of the children’s crumbs.”
Then He said unto her, “For this saying go thy way; the devil is gone out of thy daughter.”
And she went her way home, and found the child laid upon the bed, and the devil gone out.
Then He departed from thence, and came nigh unto the sea of Galilee, and went up into a mountain, and sat down there.
And great multitudes came unto Him, having with them those that were lame, blind, dumb, maimed, and many others; and they cast them down at Jesus’ feet; and He healed them.
Insomuch that the people wondered, when they saw the dumb to speak, the maimed to be whole, the lame to walk, and the blind to see: and they glorified the God of Israel.

Then Jesus called His disciples to Him and said, “I have compassion on the multitude, because they have now continued with Me three days and have nothing to eat; and I will not send them away fasting, lest they faint in the way.”
And His disciples answered Him, “From where should one have so many loaves in the wilderness, as to fill so great a multitude?”
And He asked them, “How many loaves do you have?” They said, “Seven.” (End of chapter.)
In those days, a huge crowd pulled up again, and they were mad hungry; Jesus looked at them like, “I can’t leave y’all starving.”
He said, “My heart goes out to this crowd—they’ve been with Me three days and haven’t eaten. Dedication level: max.”
“If I send them home fasting, some will pass out on the road; some of them traveled far just to vibe here.”
His disciples replied, “Lord… where are we supposed to find bread out here in this barren wasteland?”
Jesus asked them, “How many loaves you got?” They said, “Seven.”
He told the crowd to sit down; He took the seven loaves, thanked God, broke them, and told the disciples to hand them out.
They also had a few small fish; Jesus blessed them too and told His crew to distribute them.
Everyone ate till they were FULL—not nibbling, but **belly-max mode**—and they collected seven baskets of leftovers.
Around four thousand were fed. Then Jesus dismissed the crowd like, “Class dismissed.”
He and His disciples hopped into a boat and dipped to Dalmanutha.
The Pharisees showed up instantly, beef loaded, and started arguing with Him, demanding a sign from heaven.
Jesus sighed the deepest “bro…” ever and said, “Why does this generation beg for signs? No sign for you today.”
And He left them, got back in the boat, and bounced to the other side.
The disciples forgot to bring bread—only had one loaf on the boat. Very on-brand for them.
Jesus warned them, “Watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees and Herod.” (Translation: **don’t catch their bad mindset virus**.)
They whispered among themselves, “He’s saying this because we forgot bread.”
Jesus said, “Why are you like this? Why are you discussing bread? Do you still not get it?”
“You have eyes—are they on airplane mode? You have ears—are they muted?”
“Remember when I broke five loaves for five thousand—how many baskets did you pick up?” They said, “Twelve.”
“And the seven loaves for four thousand—how many baskets?” They said, “Seven.”
He said, “So how do you STILL not understand? Guys. Please.”
They came to Bethsaida, and some people brought a blind man to Jesus, begging Him to touch him.
Jesus took the blind man’s hand, led him out of the village, spit, touched his eyes, and asked, “You see anything yet?”
The man said, “I see people, but they look like walking trees.”
Jesus touched his eyes again—second try patch update—and the man’s vision fully cleared.
Jesus sent him home saying, “Don’t even go into the village.”
Jesus and His disciples walked to Caesarea Philippi; Jesus asked, “Who do people say I am?”
They said, “Some say John the Baptist, some Elijah, others one of the prophets.”
He asked them, “But YOU—who do you say I am?” Peter said, “You’re the Christ.”
Jesus told them to keep that quiet for now.
He began explaining that the Son of Man must suffer a lot, be rejected, be killed, and rise again after three days.
He said it plainly. Peter pulled Him aside to rebuke Him—bold but wrong.
Jesus turned, looked at His disciples, and told Peter, “Get behind Me, Satan. You’re not on God’s wavelength right now.”
Jesus called the crowd and His disciples, saying, “If you wanna follow Me, deny yourself, pick up your cross, and roll with Me.”
“If you try to save your own life, you’re gonna lose it; but if you lose your life for My sake and the Gospel, you’ll find it.”
“What profit is it if you gain the whole world but your soul becomes DLC lost forever?”
“Or what can someone give in exchange for their soul?”
“If you’re ashamed of Me and My words in this messed-up generation, the Son of Man will be ashamed of you when He returns in His Father’s glory with the angels.”
Jesus said, “Some of y’all standing here won’t taste death before seeing God’s kingdom pull up in full power-mode.”
Six days later, Jesus took Peter, James, and John up a mountain privately—special ops energy.
And He transformed—His clothes went blinding white, like “no detergent on earth can do this” level.
Elijah and Moses appeared and started talking with Him.
Peter—panicking as usual—said, “Rabbi, this is fire, let’s build three shelters for You, Moses, and Elijah.”
He said that because he was terrified and didn’t know what to say.
A cloud overshadowed them and a voice said, “This is My beloved Son—listen to Him.”
Suddenly, Elijah and Moses were gone; only Jesus remained.
As they descended, Jesus told them not to tell anyone until He rose from the dead.
They obeyed but whispered among themselves wondering what “rise from the dead” even meant.
They asked, “Why do the scribes say Elijah must come first?”
Jesus said, “Elijah comes to restore everything. And Scripture says the Son of Man will suffer and be rejected.”
“But I tell you—Elijah already came, and they did to him whatever they wanted, as written.”
They reached the disciples and found a huge crowd arguing with them.
When the crowd saw Jesus, they ran to Him immediately, excited.
Jesus asked the scribes, “What are you arguing with them about?”
A man from the crowd said, “Teacher, my son has an unclean spirit.”
“Whenever it takes him, it throws him down, he foams, grinds his teeth, and stiffens. I asked Your disciples—but they flopped.”
Jesus said, “O faithless generation—how long must I stay with you? Bring the boy here.”
They brought him; the spirit saw Jesus and instantly threw the boy into a seizure.
Jesus asked the father, “How long has this been happening?” He said, “Since he was a child.”
“It tries to destroy him—fire, water—everywhere. If You can do anything, please help us.”
Jesus said, “‘If You can?’ Everything is possible to the believing one.”
The father cried out, “I believe—help my unbelief!”
Seeing the crowd gathering, Jesus rebuked the spirit: “You mute, deaf spirit—I command you, come out and don’t return.”
It screamed, convulsed violently, and left. The boy lay still like a corpse.
Jesus took his hand, lifted him, and he stood.
Indoors, the disciples asked privately, “Why couldn’t we cast it out?”
Jesus said, “This kind needs prayer.”
They passed through Galilee quietly; Jesus didn’t want anyone knowing.
He taught them: “The Son of Man will be betrayed, killed, and after three days, rise again.”
They didn’t understand and were too scared to ask.
They arrived at Capernaum; Jesus asked, “What were y’all arguing about on the way?”
They stayed silent because they were arguing about who was the greatest—pure ego.
Jesus sat, called the Twelve, and said, “If you want to be first, be last and serve everyone.”
He took a child, set him among them, and held him.
“Whoever receives one child in My name receives Me, and whoever receives Me receives the One who sent Me.”
John said, “We saw someone casting out demons in Your name and stopped him because he’s not in our squad.”
Jesus said, “Don’t stop him; no one doing miracles in My name can instantly turn and badmouth Me.”
“Whoever isn’t against us is for us.”
“Anyone giving you a cup of water in My name won’t lose their reward.”
“If someone causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, better they get tossed into the sea with a giant stone necklace.”
“If your hand traps you in sin, cut it off—it’s better to enter life missing a hand than be whole and walk into fire.”
“Where the worm never dies and the fire never ends.”
“If your foot makes you sin, cut it off—it’s better to enter life lame than be tossed into fire with two good feet.”
“Where the worm never dies and the fire never ends.”
“If your eye makes you sin, pluck it out—it’s better to enter God’s kingdom with one eye than be thrown into fire with two.”
“Where the worm never dies and the fire never ends.”
“Everyone will be salted with fire.”
“Salt is good, but if the salt loses its vibe, how do you season it again? Have salt in yourselves, and live in peace with each other.”
Jesus dipped from the last location, pulled up to Judea, and the crowd gathered like free WiFi. Man started teaching again, as usual.
Then some Pharisee lawyers showed up like “heyy can we cancel marriage for ANY reason??” Testing vibes only.
Jesus hit them with the calm roast: “What did Moses say, my guy?”
They replied, “Moses allowed a divorce certificate. Basically a ‘we done’ slip.”
Jesus: “Yeah, he let you do that ’cause your hearts were hard like cheap concrete.”
“But from the jump? God made male and female. No patch updates.”
“A man leaves home, locks in with his wife…”
“…and the two become ONE codebase. Not two separate apps anymore.”
“So what God merges, don’t unpair with human nonsense.”
Later indoors, the disciples asked for the director’s cut.
Jesus: “If a man divorces and remarries, he’s cheating.”
“Same for women. No double-life DLC.”
People brought kids to Jesus for blessings, but the disciples were actin’ like bouncers.
Jesus saw it and said “Nah fam, unblock the minors. Kingdom vibes belong to people like them.”
“If you don’t receive God’s kingdom with kid-level trust? You’re cooked.”
He scooped the kids, laid hands, blessed them heavy.
Jesus was heading out when a guy sprinted up like “GOOD Teacher, how do I unlock eternal life?”
Jesus: “Why call ME good? Only God is Peak Good.”
“You know the commandments: don’t kill, don’t cheat, don’t steal, don’t cap, don’t scam, honor parents.”
Dude said, “All that? I’ve been on it since JHS.”
Jesus looked at him with love and said: “You lack one thing — go sell your stuff, bless the poor, and you’ll stack treasure in heaven. Then follow Me.”
Man’s face did a whole shutdown animation. He walked away sad because his possessions had HIM in a chokehold.
Jesus looked around: “Wow, rich people entering God’s kingdom? Hard mode.”
Disciples: “HUH??” Jesus: “Money can make people trust the bag more than God.”
“It’s easier for a camel to squeeze through a sewing needle than for a money-addicted person to enter the kingdom.”
Disciples were STRESSED: “Then who can even make it?!”
Jesus: “With humans? Impossible. With God? Everything’s possible.”
Peter said, “We left EVERYTHING for You, boss.”
Jesus: “Anyone who drops house, fam, land for Me and the gospel…”
“…gets 100x blessings now — not luxury, but community, purpose, and spiritual gains — PLUS eternal life.”
“But many who seem first now will be last, and many last will be first. Divine plot twist.”
They walked toward Jerusalem; Jesus was leading like a man who already saw the ending. Disciples were scared.
Jesus: “We’re heading to Jerusalem. I’ll be handed over to the religious leaders…”
“…mocked, spit on, whipped, killed — but three days later, I’m back.”
James and John pulled up: “Teacher, do us a favor.”
Jesus: “What you want?”
“Let us sit at Your right and left in glory — basically top-tier seats.”
Jesus: “You don’t even know the boss-level suffering you’re asking for.”
They said, “We can.” Jesus: “You WILL suffer with Me. But the seats? Not mine to assign.”
“Those spots are for whoever the Father prepared.”
The other ten heard this and got salty.
Jesus: “Gentile rulers flex authority like tyrants…”
“But not you. Whoever wants greatness must serve.”
“Whoever wants top rank must be servant of all.”
“Even I came not to be served, but to serve — and give My life as a ransom.”
They reached Jericho. A blind man, Bartimaeus, was begging roadside.
When he heard Jesus was passing, he yelled, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
People told him to shush, but he turned the volume to MAX and screamed louder.
Jesus stopped. “Call him.” The crowd switched up instantly: “Cheer up bro, He’s calling you.”
Bartimaeus YEETED his cloak, jumped up, and ran to Jesus.
Jesus asked, “What do you want Me to do?” He said, “Rabbi, I want to see.”
Jesus: “Your faith did it. Go.” Instantly the man saw and joined the squad on the road.
They came near Jerusalem—Bethphage and Bethany by the Mount of Olives. Jesus sent two disciples on a mission.
He said, “Go into the village ahead. You’ll find a colt tied up, never ridden. Untie it and bring it.”
“If anyone asks why, say, ‘The Master needs it.’ They’ll let you.”
They went and found it just as He said.
Some people asked, “Why are you untying that donkey?”
They answered exactly as Jesus told them; the people allowed it.
They brought the colt to Jesus, threw their cloaks on it, and He mounted it. True King energy.
Many spread their cloaks and leafy branches on the road, like an honor parade.
The crowd ahead and behind shouted, “Hosanna! Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!”
“Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David! Hosanna in the highest!” Crowd hype unstoppable.
Jesus entered Jerusalem, looked around the temple, then left to Bethany with the Twelve because it was late.
Next morning leaving Bethany, Jesus felt hungry.
Seeing a fig tree with leaves, He went to check for fruit but found none—just show.
He said, “No one will ever eat fruit from you again.” Disciples heard Him.
They entered Jerusalem. Jesus went into the temple courts and started driving out those selling and buying.
He prevented people from carrying goods through the temple courts.
He taught, “Is it not written, ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer for all nations’? But you have made it a den of thieves.”
The chief priests and scribes heard and began plotting to kill Him. They feared Him because the crowd was amazed at His teaching.
When evening came, He left the city.
Next morning passing by the fig tree, they saw it withered from the roots. Total checkmate.
Peter remembered and said, “Rabbi, look! The fig tree You cursed is gone!”
Jesus: “Have faith in God.”
“Truly I tell you, if anyone says to this mountain, ‘Be removed,’ and does not doubt in their heart, it will be done.”
“Therefore I tell you, whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.”
“And when you stand praying, forgive anyone you have conflict with, so that your Father in heaven may forgive you your sins.”
“Otherwise, your prayers are blocked from reaching heaven.”
They came back to Jerusalem, and Jesus entered the temple.
The chief priests, scribes, and elders confronted Him: “By what authority are You doing these things? Who gave You this power?”
Jesus said, “I will ask one question. Answer Me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.”
“John’s baptism—from heaven or from men? Tell Me.”
They debated: “If we say ‘heaven,’ He’ll ask why we didn’t believe him. If we say ‘men,’ the crowd will riot; they know John was a prophet.”
So they were afraid of the crowd.
They answered, “We don’t know.” Jesus said, “Then neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.” And He walked away.
Jesus began speaking to them in parables: “A man planted a vineyard, fenced it, dug a winepress, built a tower, and leased it to tenants. Then he went abroad.”
At harvest time, he sent a servant to the tenants to receive some of the fruit of the vineyard.
They seized him, beat him, and sent him away empty-handed.
Again, he sent another servant; they struck him on the head and treated him shamefully.
He sent still another, and they killed him. Others they beat.
The owner of the vineyard said, “What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps they will respect him.”
But the tenants said among themselves, “This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.”
They seized him, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.
What then will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the tenants and give the vineyard to others.
Have you not read this Scripture: “The stone which the builders rejected has become the cornerstone”?
This was the Lord’s doing, and it is marvelous in our eyes.
They tried to arrest him but feared the crowd; so they left him and went away.
They sent some Pharisees and Herodians to trap him: “Teacher, is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?”
Jesus, knowing their hypocrisy, said, “Why tempt me? Bring me a denarius, that I may see it.”
They brought one. He asked, “Whose image and inscription is this?” They said, “Caesar’s.”
Jesus said, “Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.” They marveled at him.
Some Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to him with a question:
“Teacher, Moses wrote that if a man dies leaving no children, his brother shall marry the widow and raise up offspring. There were seven brothers…”
“…the first married her and died, the second and the third, until all seven had her. Last of all, the woman died also.”
“In the resurrection, whose wife of the seven will she be? For they all had her.”
Jesus said to them, “You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God.”
“For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.”

“And concerning the dead, that they rise, have you not read in the book of Moses, in the burning bush passage, how God said to him, ‘I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’?”
“He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are greatly mistaken.”
One of the scribes came near and heard them arguing, and knowing he had answered well, asked him, “Which is the first commandment of all?”
Jesus answered, “The first of all is: Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one.
And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your mind, and with all your strength. This is the first commandment.
The second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. There is no other commandment greater than these.”
The scribe said to him, “Well said, Teacher; you have spoken the truth, for there is one God, and there is no other but He.
And to love Him with all the heart, understanding, and strength, and to love one’s neighbor as oneself is more than all burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
Jesus, seeing he answered wisely, said, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” And no one dared question him further.
Jesus spoke to the crowd: “Beware of the scribes, who love to walk around in long robes, greetings in the marketplaces, the best seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at feasts,”
“who devour widows’ houses, and for a pretense make long prayers. They shall receive greater condemnation.”
Jesus sat over against the treasury and watched the multitude putting in money. Many rich cast in much.
A certain poor widow came and put in two mites, which make a farthing.
He called his disciples and said, “Truly I say to you that this poor widow has put in more than all those who have cast into the treasury;”
“For all these have of their abundance cast in to the offerings of God, but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living.”
And He said to His disciples, “Beware of the scribes, who like to walk in long robes, and love greetings in marketplaces, the chief seats in synagogues, and the uppermost rooms at feasts,”
“who devour widows’ houses and for a pretense make long prayers. These will receive greater condemnation.”
And Jesus looked around at them with cold fire: “All these people flex titles and respect, but inside? Empty.”
He turned to the disciples and said, “Notice the widow’s move—she dropped everything she had. That’s peak respect energy.”
“The rich gave what they didn’t need; she gave everything she had. Heart-level flex > cash flex.”
The disciples were stunned at her courage and faith.
Jesus said, “Truly I tell you, this is what counts before God—faith, obedience, and generosity of heart. Not titles, not appearances, not flex.”
As Jesus went out of the temple, one of His disciples said, “Teacher, look! What massive stones! What buildings!”
Jesus replied, “You see all these? Truly, not one stone will be left upon another that will not be thrown down.”
As He sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew asked privately,
“Tell us, when will these things happen? What will be the sign when all this is about to be fulfilled?”
Jesus began: “Take heed that no one deceives you.
Many will come in My name, saying, ‘I am He!’ and will deceive many.
Wars will erupt, rumors of wars; don’t freak out—these must happen first, but the end is not yet.
Nation will rise against nation, kingdom against kingdom; there will be earthquakes, famines in various places. These are the beginning of birth pains.
Watch out; they will deliver you to councils, beat you in synagogues; you will stand before governors and kings for My sake, a testimony to them.
The gospel must first be preached to all nations.
When they arrest you, don’t worry beforehand about what to speak; say what is given at the time. For it is not you speaking, but the Holy Spirit.
Brother will betray brother to death, father will betray child; children will rise against parents and put them to death.
You will be hated by all for My name’s sake, but the one who endures to the end will be saved.
When you see the abomination of desolation standing where it ought not—let the reader understand—then those in Judea flee to the mountains.
Let the one on the housetop not go down or enter the house to take anything out.
Let the one in the field not turn back to take a cloak.
Woe to those who are pregnant or nursing in those days.
Pray that your flight does not occur in winter.
For those days will be tribulation, such as has not been since the beginning of the creation which God created until now, and never shall be again.
Unless the Lord had shortened those days, no flesh would be saved; but for the elect’s sake, He shortened them.
Then if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘Look, He is there!’ do not believe it.
False Christs and false prophets will rise, showing signs and wonders to deceive, if possible, even the elect.
Take heed; I have told you all things beforehand.
But in those days, after that tribulation, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its light,
the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers in the heavens will be shaken.
Then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
He will send angels and gather His elect from the four winds, from the ends of the earth to the ends of heaven.
Now learn a parable from the fig tree: When its branch becomes tender and sprouts leaves, you know that summer is near.
So also, when you see these things happening, know that it is near, even at the doors.
Truly I say to you, this generation will not pass away till all these things are accomplished.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will not pass away.
But of that day or hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but the Father.
Take heed, watch, and pray; for you do not know when the time is.
It is like a man going on a journey: He left his house, gave authority to his servants, and commanded the doorkeeper to watch.
Watch therefore—for you do not know when the master of the house will come, at evening, midnight, cockcrow, or morning—
lest coming suddenly he finds you sleeping.
What I say to you, I say to all: Watch.
After two days it was the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread. The chief priests and scribes sought how to arrest Jesus secretly and kill Him.
They said, “Not during the feast, or the people may riot.”
Jesus was at Bethany in the house of Simon the leper. A woman came with an alabaster jar of expensive perfume of pure nard. She broke it and poured it on His head.
Some were indignant: “Why waste this perfume?
It could have been sold for over three hundred denarii and given to the poor!” They scolded her.
Jesus said, “Leave her alone. Why do you trouble her? She has done a beautiful thing for Me.
You always have the poor with you, but you do not always have Me.
She has done what she could. She has anointed My body beforehand for burial.
Truly, wherever this gospel is preached throughout the world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”
Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went to the chief priests to betray Him.
They were glad and promised to give him money. He sought an opportunity to betray Him.
On the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they killed the Passover lamb, His disciples said to Him, “Where do You want us to go and prepare that You may eat the Passover?”
He sent two disciples, saying, “Go into the city, a man will meet you carrying a pitcher of water; follow him.
Wherever he enters, say to the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says, Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?’
He will show you a large upper room furnished; prepare it there.”
The disciples went and did as Jesus commanded, and they prepared the Passover.
When evening came, He arrived with the twelve.
As they reclined and were eating, Jesus said, “Truly I say to you, one of you will betray Me, one who is eating with Me.”
They were sorrowful and began to say to Him, one by one, “Surely not I?”
He said to them, “It is one of the twelve, one who dips with Me in the dish.
The Son of Man goes, as it is written of Him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would have been better for him not to have been born.”
As they were eating, He took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “Take; this is My body.”
He took the cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, and they all drank.
He said, “This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.
Truly I say to you, I will not drink again of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.”
After singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Jesus said to them, “You will all be offended because of Me this night. For it is written: ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’
But after I am risen, I will go before you into Galilee.”
Peter said, “Even if all are offended, I will never be offended.”
Jesus said to him, “Truly I say to you, this day—yes, tonight, before the rooster crows twice—you will deny Me three times.”
But he insisted more vehemently: “Even if I must die with You, I will not deny You.” And all the disciples said likewise.
They came to a place called Gethsemane. He said to His disciples, “Sit here while I pray.”
He took Peter, James, and John with Him and began to be greatly distressed and troubled.
He said, “My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death. Stay here and watch.”
He went a little farther, fell to the ground, and prayed that, if possible, the hour might pass from Him,
saying, “Abba, Father, all things are possible for You. Remove this cup from Me; nevertheless, not what I will, but what You will.”
He came and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, “Simon, are you asleep? Could you not watch one hour?
Watch and pray, lest you enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
Again He went away and prayed, saying the same words.
Again He came and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy; they did not know what to answer Him.
He came the third time and said to them, “Sleep on now and take your rest. It is enough; the hour has come. Behold, the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
Rise! Let us go; behold, he who betrays Me is at hand.”
Immediately, while He was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a crowd with swords and clubs from the chief priests, scribes, and elders.
Now he who betrayed Him had given them a sign: “Whomever I kiss, He is the One. Seize Him and lead Him away safely.”
When he came, he immediately went to Him, saying, “Rabbi!” and kissed Him.
They laid hands on Him and arrested Him.
One of those who stood by drew his sword, struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his ear.
Jesus said to them, “Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs to take Me?
I was daily with you in the temple teaching, and you did not seize Me. But the Scriptures must be fulfilled.”
They all forsook Him and fled.
A young man followed Him, having a linen cloth thrown around his naked body. They laid hold on him,
but he left the cloth and fled naked.
They led Jesus away to the high priest; and all the chief priests, elders, and scribes were gathered.
Peter followed at a distance to the high priest’s courtyard; he sat with the servants and warmed himself by the fire.
The chief priests and the whole council sought testimony against Jesus to put Him to death, but found none.
Many gave false testimony against Him, but their testimonies did not agree.
Some rose up and bore false witness against Him, saying,
“We heard Him say, ‘I will destroy this temple made with hands, and in three days I will build another not made with hands.’”
But even so, their testimony did not agree.
The high priest stood up in the midst and asked Jesus, “Do You answer nothing? What is it these testify against You?”
But He kept silent and answered nothing. Again the high priest asked Him, “Are You the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?”
Jesus said, “I am. And you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.”
Then the high priest tore his clothes and said, “What further need do we have of witnesses?
You have heard the blasphemy. What do you think?” They all condemned Him as deserving death.
Some began to spit on Him, blindfolded Him, struck Him with their fists, saying, “Prophesy!” And the servants received Him with blows.
As Peter sat in the courtyard, a servant girl came to him, “You were with Jesus the Galilean!”
But he denied it before them all, saying, “I do not know what you are saying.”
When he went out to the gateway, another saw him and said, “You are with Jesus of Nazareth!”
He again denied it, with an oath: “I do not know the man!”
After a little while, those standing by came and said to Peter, “Surely you are one of them, for you are a Galilean!”
He began to curse and swear, “I do not know the man!” Immediately a rooster crowed the second time.
Peter remembered the word Jesus had said: “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.” And he broke down and wept.
Immediately, in the morning, the chief priests held a council with the elders and scribes and led Jesus away to Pilate.
Pilate asked Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?” He answered, “You say so.”
The chief priests accused Him of many things, but He answered nothing.
Pilate asked again, “Do You not answer? See how many charges they bring against You!”
But Jesus still answered nothing, much to Pilate’s amazement.
Now at the feast, Pilate was used to releasing one prisoner, anyone they asked.
There was one called Barabbas, thrown in for insurrection and murder.
The crowd came and began to ask Pilate to do as he always did for them.
Pilate asked, “Do you want me to release the King of the Jews?”
For he knew the chief priests had delivered Him out of envy.
But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release Barabbas instead.
Pilate answered, “What then shall I do with Him you call King of the Jews?”
They shouted, “Crucify Him!”
Pilate said, “Why? What evil has He done?” But they shouted all the more, “Crucify Him!”
Pilate, wanting to please the crowd, released Barabbas to them, and delivered Jesus to be crucified.
The soldiers led Him away into the hall called Praetorium; they called together the whole cohort.
They clothed Him in purple and twisted a crown of thorns, putting it on Him.
They began to salute Him, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
They struck His head with a reed, spat on Him, and bowed down in mockery.
When they had mocked Him, they took off the purple robe, put His own clothes on Him, and led Him out to crucify Him.
They compelled a passerby, Simon of Cyrene, to carry His cross.
They brought Him to Golgotha, which is “Place of a Skull.”
They offered Him wine mingled with myrrh, but He did not take it.
They crucified Him and divided His garments, casting lots on them to see what each would take.
It was the third hour when they crucified Him.
The inscription of His accusation was written: “THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
They crucified two robbers with Him, one on the right, the other on the left.
[Some manuscripts omit this verse.]
Those passing by derided Him, shaking their heads and saying, “Ha! You who would destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, save Yourself and come down from the cross!”
Likewise, the chief priests and scribes mocked Him, saying, “He saved others; He cannot save Himself.
Let the Christ, the King of Israel, descend now from the cross, that we may see and believe.”
Those crucified with Him also reviled Him.
At the sixth hour, darkness fell over the whole land until the ninth hour.
At the ninth hour, Jesus cried out with a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?” which means, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”
Some of those standing by heard it and said, “Behold, He is calling Elijah!”
One ran, filled a sponge with sour wine, put it on a reed, and gave Him to drink, saying, “Wait, let’s see if Elijah comes to take Him down.”
Jesus cried out again with a loud voice and yielded up His spirit.
The veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
The centurion who stood opposite Him, seeing how He cried out and gave up His spirit, said, “Truly, this man was the Son of God!”
There were also women watching from afar: Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.
When He was in Galilee, they followed Him and ministered to Him; many other women came up with Him to Jerusalem.
Now when evening had come, because it was the preparation day, that is, the day before the Sabbath,
Joseph of Arimathea, a prominent council member who awaited the kingdom of God, boldly went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body.
Pilate marveled that He was already dead; summoning the centurion, he asked if He had died.
When confirmed, Pilate gave the body to Joseph.
He bought a linen cloth, took Him down, wrapped Him, and laid Him in a tomb that had been hewn out of rock. He rolled a stone against the entrance.
Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses saw where He was laid.
When Sabbath finally clocked out, Mary Magdalene, Mary mother of James, and Salome pulled up with spices—basically the ancient-version self-care kit for honoring Jesus.
At crack-of-dawn o’clock in the morning, sunrise hitting like a soft filter, they went straight to the tomb.
On the way they were like, “Hold up… who’s bench-pressing that stone for us? ’Cause we not built for that.”
But when they looked up, the stone—big as it was—had already been rolled away.
They stepped inside, and boom—there’s a young dude in a clean, bright fit sitting on the right side. They instantly went from “morning stroll” to “system update required.”
He said, “Relax. I know you’re looking for Jesus of Nazareth—the crucified One. He’s not here. He got up. Check the spot; it’s empty.”
“Now go tell His disciples—*and Peter* especially—that He’s already heading to Galilee. You’ll see Him there like He told you.”
They dipped from the tomb shaking, brain-lagging, emotion-crashing, and kept quiet at first ’cause fear had them on airplane mode.
First appearance? Mary Magdalene—the one Jesus freed from seven demons. She had the exclusive drop.
She ran to tell the squad, who were busy grieving like their hope app just crashed.
They heard her say she saw Him alive but didn’t buy it. L mans activity.
After that, He showed up to two others walking outside the city, but in a different look—like a skin change moment.
They told the rest, and again… disbelief. The team was moving like their faith had low battery.
Later, Jesus pulled up on the eleven while they were eating and literally called them out for their unbelief and stubborn vibes. The man resurrected and still had to fight spiritual laziness.
Then He said, “Go everywhere. Tell everyone the gospel. No region left on ‘seen.’”
“Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved; whoever does not believe will be condemned.”
“And signs will follow believers like verified badges: they’ll cast out demons in My name, speak new languages,”
handle snakes; and if they drink poison, it won’t cook them. They’ll lay hands on sick people, and the sick will bounce back.”
After Jesus finished giving the mission briefing, He ascended straight up to heaven and sat at God’s right hand like the rightful King He is.
The disciples went everywhere preaching, and Jesus co-signed their work with signs that followed—basically Divine receipts. Amen.
